procedure.description: revascularization of the femoral-popliteal artery with atherectomy and stent placement

denial.carcText: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer.
denial.text: Copperfield Health denied the claim for CPT 37227 (revascularization of the femoral-popliteal artery with atherectomy and stent placement) with date of service 2026-05-06. CARC 56: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer. Payer remark: Atherectomy is considered investigational for femoropopliteal disease.

criteria.text: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (ischemic rest pain, non-healing ulcer, or gangrene, Rutherford 4 to 6); or lifestyle-limiting claudication (Rutherford 3) that has failed at least 12 weeks of supervised exercise therapy and optimal medical therapy.
Hemodynamic confirmation: ankle-brachial index 0.4 or less, toe pressure below 30 mmHg, or TcPO2 below 30 mmHg for limb-threatening ischemia (ankle-brachial index below 0.9 for claudication).
Imaging (duplex, CT angiography, or angiography) demonstrating a femoropopliteal stenosis of 50 percent or more, or an occlusion, amenable to endovascular treatment.
Optimal medical therapy documented: an antiplatelet agent, a statin, and smoking cessation or cessation counseling.

chart.text: Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Here with a cough and congestion for 6 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Blood pressure check. 130 over 81 today, 120 over 93 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 8 weeks.
Vitamin D came back 14. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Left heel ulcer 2.4 by 1.6 centimeters, pale base, no granulation tissue after 10 weeks of weekly debridement and offloading. Pedal pulses not palpable.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

69 year old man referred by podiatry for the left leg. Diabetic 10 years, hypertension, prior coronary stent. Discussed endovascular versus bypass; endovascular first given the anatomy. His history otherwise: hypothyroidism on levothyroxine. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Never smoked, occasional beer, lives alone. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Left heel ulcer for 3 months that will not heal despite offloading and weekly wound care, and rest pain in the left foot at night relieved by hanging it off the bed. Rutherford 5. On aspirin 81 and atorvastatin 80. Quit smoking 9 weeks ago after 35 years; counseled again today and offered nicotine replacement.
Arterial studies. Ankle-brachial index left 0.30, right 0.87. Left toe pressure 26 mmHg. Monophasic waveforms at the left popliteal and tibial levels.

CT angiography with runoff: left superficial femoral artery occluded over 16 centimeters from the mid thigh to the adductor canal, reconstitution of the above-knee popliteal artery, two-vessel runoff via the anterior tibial and peroneal. Contralateral mild disease. Aortoiliac segments patent.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
A1c came back 6.5. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. He is motivated.

Back to review the imaging. Plan left superficial femoral artery recanalization with atherectomy and stent, outpatient. Risks reviewed including embolization and need for bypass. Vitals today 132 over 71, pulse 71.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.5, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 7 years.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.
Pre-procedure visit. Creatinine 0.9, hold metformin, hydration protocol. Consent signed.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 213, LDL 117, HDL 59, triglycerides 159. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 56 denial can be answered from the record.
